title: AI Agent Controller
tagline: A desk dock and detachable controller for running AI coding agents: glance, flick, approve, speak.
status_text: Building: the dock screens run in a simulator; dock board flashed; display test next
tags: ESP32-S3, LVGL, Python, Whisper, Claude Code, CadQuery, 3D printing
hero_alt: Concept render of the agent controller: a small screen on a hinged lid, a ribbed base, three large keys and a joystick block that pivots

timeline.title: The dock's screens run in a simulator
timeline.summary: The screens are built with LVGL: the agent list, a detail page, approvals, a voice screen, toasts and a Disconnected banner. They run in a window on the Mac, driven by the real companion app, and the same code already compiles for the dock board. Each row is named after its task, then its project folder.

images.alt: Simulator: an approval request with four choices
Simulator: the detail page for a finished session
Simulator: the detail page for a session that is still working

timeline.title: The app's controls match the reference
timeline.summary: Stick right opens a session, stick left goes back, and only Send confirms an approval. Resting the stick on a session brings its window to the front. Checked on the Mac Mini with real Claude Code sessions.

timeline.title: Parts on the bench, first firmware on the dock board
timeline.summary: Most of the parts arrived. The dock board (ESP32-S3) was flashed from the Mac Mini and reports 16 MB of flash and 8 MB of PSRAM, as ordered. The display and touch test is written and waits for jumper wires.

timeline.title: Rev 3: the joystick block pivots
timeline.summary: A full re-check of the reference product. The joystick block now swings out 90° under your thumb, the keys became large plates, and the plan and blueprint were rebuilt around that. A 3D concept model places every part and checks that nothing collides.

timeline.title: Approving Claude Code from the device
timeline.summary: The companion app now follows every Claude Code session through its hooks. A real permission request popped up on the fake device, and one key press approved it.

timeline.title: Rev 2: dock + detachable controller
timeline.summary: Rigid controller bar that charges on the dock, USB + Wi-Fi data paths, voice pipeline and platform plug-in plan.

Exploded view of the dock with every part labeled
Exploded view of the controller bar with every part labeled

timeline.title: Rev 1: parametric clamshell
timeline.summary: First printed-shell design with automatic fit checks. The checks showed the joystick was too tall, which led to rev 2.

timeline.title: Companion app works end to end
timeline.summary: A task sent over WebSocket runs Claude Code and streams tool and done events back to the device.
